items.actClause: AN ACT to amend a chapter of the laws of 2015, amending the not-for-profit corporation law relating to allowing certain entities to convert their status of filing as a not-for-profit organization to a for-profit entity, as proposed in legislative bills numbers S.5848 and A.8116, in relation to providing for the repeal of such provisions upon the expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Amd §2, Chap of 2015 (as proposed in S.5848 & A.8116)
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5996

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend a chapter of the laws of 2015, amending the
not-for-profit corporation law relating to allowing certain entities
to convert their status of filing as a not-for-profit organization to
a for-profit entity, as proposed in legislative bills numbers S.5848
and A.8116, in relation to providing for the repeal of such provisions
upon the expiration thereof

PURPOSE:

To amend chapters of the laws of 2015 to sunset the chapter of 2015
after 180 days.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph 4 of the not-for-profit corporation law, as
amended by chapter of the laws of 2015, amending the not-for-profit
law relating to allowing certain entities to convert their status of
filing as a not-for-profit organization to a for-profit entity to
repeal this act within 180 days of the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Although the underlying law is limited in its application this
amendment would further limit the application of the chapter of the
laws of 2015. This change would ensure that the certain entities have
the time that are needed for the Attorney General to review and opine
on the application as well as limit the pool of entities who could
avail themselves to the conversion.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as
a chapter of the laws of 2015, amending the not-for-profit,
corporation law, in relation to allowing certain entities to convert
their status of filing as a not-for-profit organization to a
for-profit entity as proposed in legislative bills numbers S.5848 and
A.8116, takes effect.

A.actClause: AN ACT to allow certain entities to convert their status of filing as a not-for-profit organization to a for-profit entity; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5996A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to allow certain entities to convert their
status of filing as a not-for-profit organization to a for-profit
entity; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof

PURPOSE:  To allow certain entities to convert their status as a
not-for-profit organization to a for-profit entity

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Section 104 of the not-for-profit corporation law by
adding a new paragraph (h) to allow certain entities to convert its
filing from a not-for-profit corporation to a for-profit corporation
if the incorporator submits a sworn statement and outlines the
requirements for the sworn statement.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:  Enterprising business entrepreneurs are often advised
to incorporate a business to protect personal assets from loss
suffered by the business in the event of lawsuits. Incorporation of a
business however, often carries high costs, including legal fees which
can be too costly for someone with only a dollar and a dream. To save
money, entrepreneurs sometimes choose "do it yourself routes" and make
mistakes that have significant consequences on the outcome of the
business venture. When this occurs, our rules and regulations should
provide a process for correction of mistakes.

In December 2000, Patricia Smith took the first step to her dream of
owning her own business in the health care industry and filed
documents to incorporate Sweet P Home Care. With little money to
invest in legal counsel she used standard forms and completed the
information by handwriting the necessary information. While intending
to run a for-profit business which is in fact how she ran her business
after filing the incorporation forms she mistakenly filed as a
not-for-profit corporation.

In 2006 Sweet P Homecare commenced operation. Sweet P Home Care
provides care to infirmed children who are chronically ill. Currently
it employs 10 full time employees and contracts with 300 additional
nurse independent contractors to perform services for Sweet P Home
Care's clients. Since 2006 Sweet P has conducted it's business as a
for-profit paying taxes in every year of operation. Realizing its
mistake Sweet Pea has spoken with the Department of State and the
Attorney General's office and been informed that the only way for the
mistake to be corrected is through a changes in law.

Currently, our incorporation registration laws do not provide a
process to correct errors that can be made during the business
registration process. For example, when an intended for profit
business is inadvertently registered as a not-for-profit.

Enactment of this law will establish a process for businesses who
inadvertently register under the wrong classification to convert to


the correct business status and allow for Sweet P Home Care to correct
the mistake.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: A new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the state

LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately and shall
expire and be deemed repealed one hundred eighty days after such date.
